account: Today is day 1, shortly after eleven. I attended my scheduled mill grain inspection and found 76 hay bales offered at two emeralds each in the mill stall. That establishes the offered stock, but not whether deliveries are running normally. Several townsfolk have repeated an unusual report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Their accounts name the baker, freight, and innkeeper, with some also naming the builder and our neighbour. One report said the innkeeper carried a sack of bread. I have not witnessed the reported change or heard a clear firsthand explanation, so I cannot yet say what changed, who arranged it, or why. It may concern deliveries or river crossings, but that is only a possibility, not an established fact. I asked the secretary to find someone with firsthand knowledge. Separately, the secretary reports no correspondence has reached her. Our neighbour has confirmed tea at fifteen and says nothing is needed for our ordinary eighteen o'clock meeting at town hall. There is no evidence connecting that meeting with the bakery reports. My remaining appointments are lunch at home at twelve, council letters at thirteen, tea at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, the town hall meeting at eighteen, and home at nineteen.
